subject: Non-Euclidean distances: Dynamic userdist with Individual-x-Site Learned Response and Terrain Ruggedness Index

messages.author: b6ebbabd9b16dd3f
messages.subject: Non-Euclidean distances: Dynamic userdist with Individual-x-Site Learned Response and Terrain Ruggedness Index
parts:
Hello all,

 

I am working on a study in Switzerland, where we employ camera traps to calculate the density of lynx per 100km2. So far, I have identified the site-specific learned response model Mbk as the best model using predefined models (while keeping the parameter sigma constant). As in mountainous landscape lynx movements are strongly influenced by the topography of the terrain, we are investigating the non-euclidean distances in secr;

 

I first used static userdist to add barriers to my mask (lakes), and now I'm attempting to perform a dynamic userdist. Specifically, I aim to model densities by accounting for non-Euclidean ecological distances determined by e.g. the Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI).

 

To account for the TRI, I believe I should use the code provided in the example 5 ‘Habitat model for connectivity’ of the dynamic userdist section in “Non-Euclidean distances in secr 4.6”, Murray Efford, 2023:

 

fit5 <- secr.fit(lynx_capthist, mask = Mask_NonEucDist_Lakes_1000b,

trace = FALSE,

details = list(userdist = fn2, fastproximity = FALSE),

model = list(D ~ 1, g0~bk, noneuc ~ TRI),

fixed = list(sigma = 1))

 

However, I am uncertain about the appropriate function to employ in userdist. Here the function fn2 (p.6 and written below) was used in the model to acknowledge that the “scale of movement σ depends on locations of both home-range centre and detector”. But I am not sure to understand the link between the function fn2 and the noneuc ~ TRI, what function should I use in the userdist when my aim is to account for how the terrain ruggedness could affect the lynx movements and detection probability…?

 

Also before trying fit5 above, I tried the fit2 (below) to test the fn2 function alone, but the loglik returns only NA, even when I change the starting value of the sigma parameter. However, I noticed that when I remove the “fixed = list(sigma = 1)the loglik returns values, and I “just” get the warning message “In secr.fit(lynx_capthist, mask = Mask_NonEucDist_Lakes_1000b, details = list(userdist = fn2,  : at least one variance calculation failed”.


Here is the code of the function (fn2) and the fit2:

#2:Scale of movement σ depends on locations of both home-range centre and detector

fn2 <- function (xy1, xy2, mask) {

  if (missing(xy1)) return("noneuc")

  xy1 <- addCovariates(xy1, mask)

  xy2 <- addCovariates(xy2, mask)

  sig1 <- as.numeric(covariates(xy1)$noneuc) 

  sig2 <- as.numeric(covariates(xy2)$noneuc) 

  euc <- edist(xy1, xy2)

  # sigma(x,y) at detectors

  # sigma(x,y) at mask points

  sig <- outer (sig1, sig2, FUN = function(s1, s2) (s1 + s2)/2)

  euc / sig }

fit2 <- secr.fit(lynx_capthist, mask = Mask_NonEucDist_Lakes_1000b,

trace = FALSE,

                 details = list(userdist = fn2,fastproximity = FALSE), 

                 model = noneuc ~ x + y + x2 + y2 + xy,

                 fixed = list(sigma = 1))

 

 

In summary my questions are the following:

  • How can I correctly implement dynamic userdist to test my hypothesis that non-euclidean distances are related to terrain ruggedness?
  • In the fit5, how does the function fn2 relate to noneuc~TRI, and is fn2 suitable for the aim of this study?
  • Why does the loglik return only NA when using fit2 with a fixed sigma, and how can I overcome this issue?
  • Why is sigma fixed in every example of the dynamic userdist in the referenced material, and is this necessary ?

Thanks in advance for your help!

 

Inès

messages.subject: Re: Non-Euclidean distances: Dynamic userdist with Individual-x-Site Learned Response and Terrain Ruggedness Index
parts:
• You seem to be following in the footsteps of Sutherland et al., so do read the Appendix to "Non-Euclidean distances in secr 4.6". That has a non-euclidean distance function 'userdfn1' that may be appropriate.
  • 'fn2' averages the predicted sigma values at the start and end of a potential path; this is probably not what you want.
  • logLik NA may happen for many reasons, including bad starting values and impossible (e.g., infinite) non-euclidean distances.
  • sigma is notionally fixed at a known value in the model (1), and the machinery of non-euclidean distance in effect  models variation in sigma relative to that fixed value. This is partly explained in the Notes of the pdf.

parts:
Thank you Murray. I'll be sure to have a look at the materials you've pointed out.

Regarding the fixed sigma value, I have a follow-up question: Would it be methodologically sound to use the sigma value derived from the simpler model (D~1, g0~bk, sigma~1) for this specific study area as the fixed sigma in the more complex non-euc model? I am considering this because it could serve as a biologically relevant and study-specific baseline around which variations due to non-Euclidean factors can be modeled, (as my model wasn't converging well with fixed sigma =1). Would this approach be in line with the framework you've described? And would this necessitate a corresponding adjustment in λ0 to prevent biologically implausible results (as indicated in your notes)?

Inès

messages.subject: Re: Non-Euclidean distances: Dynamic userdist with Individual-x-Site Learned Response and Terrain Ruggedness Index
parts: The detection function concerns only r = d/sigma, as explained. As I think about it: "non-euclidean" distances mess with the definition of d, putting it on an arbitrary new scale, and fixing sigma to a constant ensures that r varies in proportion to the new d (and is controlled by the model for noneuc, not the model for sigma). Whether sigma=1 or anything else is not material, except that it will change the absolute value of coefficients (and required starting values).
